decision.title: DTD processing: external subset, external entities, validation (packets 7.14a, 7.14b)

body.p: , after , , , , , , , , . Replaces 's "the external subset is not read" and "external parsed entities are skipped in content".

item.p: Header, additive (include/sxml/xml.h): an entity resolver (sxml_xml_entity_resolver: resolve and release over sxml_xml_external_entity_request → sxml_xml_external_entity), named per parse in sxml_xml_parse_request.entity_resolver. The null resolver (a zeroed request) reads nothing outside the input, as before. The request carries the purpose (external subset, parameter entity, general entity), name, system and public identifiers and the system identifier resolved against the base URI of the entity holding the declaration (4.2.2). xml.h cannot name processor.h's resource resolver (processor.h includes xml.h), so the parser has its own small interface and the processor adapts its resolver to it.

Grammar (, grammars/xml): the start rule also reads the external subset and external parsed entities, each after a marker the builder writes (U+0001 and a letter: no [2] Char, so a document never takes these alternatives, and the builder refuses one without a root). New: ([30], [31]), external_parsed_entity ([78]), ([77]), include_section ([62]), ([63], or a parameter-entity keyword), ignored_section_contents ([64], [65], scanner token ignored_text), entity values with parameter-entity references in external DTD text. The internal subset stays strict (WFC: PEs in Internal Subset in the grammar).

What the grammar cannot express is a loop with explicit stacks (), as the task allowed: a declaration with a parameter-entity reference outside its literals matches its production only after expansion, so the scanner returns it as one token; the builder replaces the references (4.4.8, one space on each side, the replacement texts' own references too, with quote state and an explicit stack of open entities in the parser's expansion array) and parses the result again as the external subset in a frame of its own. The same loop includes a reference in an entity value in the literal (4.4.5: character and parameter-entity references recognized again, general ones kept). A conditional section whose keyword is a reference is read as ignored text by the grammar; the builder reads keyword, '[' and contents from the replacement text and the rest of the section (the '[' may come from the entity, a validity matter only) and parses an included section again. A missing '>' that comes from an entity (Proper Declaration/PE Nesting) ends the token at the next markup.

Reading: the external subset after the internal subset (2.8), through a parameter entity named "[dtd]" (no Name, so unreachable); external parameter entities where referenced; external parsed entities in content (parsed after the entity marker, the tree cached per parse as an internal entity's is, frames of a new kind whose walk root is the entity). Each external entity is asked once per parse, decoded as a document is (Appendix F; its text declaration must agree with the bytes), its byte order mark dropped, U+0000 refused, line ends normalized in the copy (2.11); a 1.1 document's entities follow 1.1 (restricted characters, NEL), and an entity of a 1.0 document must not declare 1.1 (XML 1.1, 4.3.4). An entity the resolver does not deliver is not read (4.4.3, 5.1: later entity and attribute-list declarations are skipped as for an unread parameter entity). Every external text counts against maximum_entity_expansion_byte_count at each inclusion.
WFC: Entity Declared where it applies (no DTD, internal subset without references, standalone="yes") also refuses an entity declared in the external subset or in a parameter entity (4.1).

Measured (tests/xml_conformance_test.c, now parsing every case with a file resolver; the 1.0 selection with ENTITIES other than "none" is a third group): standalone 1.0 unchanged 601/175/948; external 1.0 0 run before, now valid 127/127, invalid 54/54 (well-formed), not-wf 66/66, error 18; XML 1.1 not-wf 140/169 to 169/169 ('s 29). The remaining parts (the processor's resource kind, trust-external, the drivers, the CLI, DTD validation) follow in this record.

Validation (7.14b) is schema validation (no second content-model engine): src/dtd.c writes the DTD as XSD documents, one per namespace (names resolve through the root element's xmlns attributes and the DTD's xmlns defaults; content models become model groups, attribute types simple types: ID, IDREF(S), ENTITY(IES), NMTOKEN(S), NOTATION, enumerations; an element referred to but not declared gets a type that refuses it). src/schema_from_dtd.c compiles them and runs a schema validator without a result tree; the parser sends its events to it as well (a tee). The constraints about declarations themselves (Root Element Type, Standalone Document Declaration, the PE nesting ones, Unique Element Type Declaration, Unique Notation Name, One ID per Element Type, ID Attribute Default, Notation Declared, No Duplicate Types and Tokens, Entity Declared, Fixed Attribute Default) the parser checks and reports through the hook, code xml-validity. Public, additive: xml.h's sxml_xml_validator hook (sxml_xml_parse_request.validator); schema.h's sxml_dtd_validator (memory_requirements, initialize, finalize, create, destroy, as_xml_validator, get_outcome); processor.h's resource kind SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_EXTERNAL_ENTITY (form BYTES) and sxml_processor_entity_resolver, which adapts the processor's resource resolver for a parse.

Tree: element content whitespace (a declared element-only content model) makes no text node (XDM 4.0, 7.5.7.3); unparsed entities keep absolute system identifiers, so fn:unparsed-entity-uri and fn:unparsed-entity-public-id work (replaces 's "unparsed entities are not reported").

fn:doc and fn:parse-xml (F&O 4.0, 17.1.1 and 17.2.1): the loader parses with an entity resolver over the evaluation's resource resolver. trust-external defaults to false, so a document that refers to an external DTD or entity raises FODC0016 (the 4.0 incompatibility the specification names); dtd-validation=true validates and raises FODC0007 (also for a document without a DTD, 2.8). FODC0013 stays for XInclude. XSLT's fn:document and stylesheet modules read external entities through the resolver. The CLI parses its input files with the null resolver, so it never reads an external entity (); a query reads one only through trust-external=true.

Measured: DTD validation of xmlconf: standalone valid 594 of 594 valid, invalid 173 of 173 invalid; external valid 127 of 127, invalid 54 of 54. XT40 8,861 to 8,931 passed (release, whole suite, none lost); dtd cases 68 of 79 (86 %, under the 90 % gate): base-uri-051/051a/051b need an element base URI from the entity (tree.h; Proposed), unparsed-entity-05 to 08 need unparsed entities kept by xsl:copy-of (Proposed), error-1370a, 1380a and 1380b raise the wrong code without a focus, id-043 needs a parse-xml source in the driver. QT4 (release): fn-doc XQ40 69 to 73, XP40 63 to 67; fn-parse-xml XQ40 46 to 53, XP40 35 to 42; none lost. Left for the QT4 driver (its files were others' work in progress): claiming infoset-dtd and dtd-validation-option, environment sources read with the entity resolver, and supports-dtd-validation true in src/system_property.c with the feature claim. Fuzzing: tests/fuzz/dtd_fuzz.c, 20 minutes, clean after one fix.
